verdict_summary: FAIL. The transform and hard-mask bookkeeping are exact, but the authoritative final pixels show no two-segment limb: only a severed shoulder stump and detached shard survive. The target is not integrated in Unity, the fresh engine evidence is the wrong fighter, the score is 33/100 with a 0 floor, and the blind result is 0/6.
single_biggest_remaining_visual_gap: The accepted silhouette has no connected shoulder-to-elbow-to-grip arm: protection destroys the elbow and entire steep return, leaving a shoulder stump and floating far-low shard instead of one anatomical V and its uninterrupted pale wedge.
round017_exact_actionable_prescription: Keep the three anchors fixed at shoulder (604,472), elbow (370,845), and grip (450,625), but change exactly one constraint: inside only the existing target triangle and limb corridors, stop treating overlapping hilt/rear-leg protection pixels as immutable. Define the Round017 editable mask as the current final mask union the currently protected pixels inside the closed triangle [(604,472),(370,845),(450,625)] dilated by 62 px, then restore only a 24 px-radius disk centered on grip (450,625) after compositing; freeze every pixel outside that revised mask. Composite one connected arm whose changed pixels form one 8-connected component from shoulder to elbow to the restored grip disk and whose two segments bound a clear pale head-sized wedge. This is the smallest viable constraint relaxation; moving no anchors preserves all geometry while unfreezing only the local pixels that currently make the topology impossible.
